notes: θεός carries the supplied *there is* under rule 68, the clause expressing no subject; within the anarthrous numeral-plus-noun predicate the noun is the carrier on rule 58's reasoning. Putting *there is* on εἷς remains defensible and the unit note records it.
The two εἷς tokens are kept on their own English *one* tokens rather than sharing one unit (rule 26).
θεοῦ takes *between God* under rule 21's determinerless clause, the supplied case preposition riding with the genitive.

*himself* is folded onto ἄνθρωπος as a rule 7 pronoun helper, rule 11 keeping the italics from deciding it; marking it `added` under rule 5, as rule 105 does where a substantival article carries a supplied appositional word, remains defensible — but no article carries it here.
Χριστός and Ἰησοῦς are split under rule 28 rather than given a shared head.
